A rotary cutter unit (6) for an agricultural mower (2) comprises a housing (14) that carries a rotary bearing (18) having an axis of rotation (X), and a rotor assembly (20) that is supported by the bearing for rotation relative to the housing about the axis of rotation. The rotor assembly includes a shaft (24) that extends through the bearing, a drive input element (28) at an input end of the shaft for transmitting rotary drive to the shaft and a drive output element (32) at an output end (22) of the shaft to receive rotary drive from the shaft. A frangible element (40) comprising a weakened portion of the shaft (24) is provided between the drive input element and the drive output element, which is configured to break when subjected to an excessive load so as to interrupt the transmission of rotary drive between the drive input element and the drive output element. A retention mechanism (44) is provided, which prevents separation of the drive output element from the housing when the frangible element breaks but permits rotation of the drive output element relative to the housing. The retention mechanism includes a retention element (46, 48) that extends substantially radially between the drive output element (32) and the housing (14) to restrict axial movement between the drive output element and the housing.

A rotary cutting assembly (6) for an agricultural mower (2) includes a housing (14) fitted with a rotary bearing (18) defining a rotational axis (X). A rotor assembly (20) is mounted in the bearing so that it can turn relative to the housing about that axis. The rotor assembly has a shaft (24) passing through the bearing, a drive input component (28) positioned at an input end of the shaft to deliver rotational drive to the shaft, and a drive output component (32) positioned at an output end (22) of the shaft to receive that rotational drive.

Between the drive input component and the drive output component there is a breakable part (40), formed by a weakened section of the shaft (24). This part is designed to fracture under an excessive load, thereby stopping the transfer of rotary drive from the drive input component to the drive output component. A retaining arrangement (44) is also included. When the breakable part fractures, this arrangement stops the drive output component from separating from the housing while still allowing the drive output component to rotate relative to the housing. The retaining arrangement has a retaining member (46, 48) extending generally outward in a radial direction between the drive output component (32) and the housing (14), thereby limiting axial displacement between the drive output component and the housing.
outputs.L3:
A rotary cutter unit for an agricultural mower includes a housing that supports a rotary bearing and a rotor assembly mounted for rotation about a defined rotational axis. The housing provides structural support for the cutter unit and maintains the alignment of the rotating components during operation.

The rotor assembly includes a shaft that extends through the rotary bearing. At one end of the shaft, a drive input element is provided for receiving rotary power, for example from a gearbox, belt drive, or other drive transmission of the mower. At the opposite end of the shaft, a drive output element is provided for transmitting rotary motion to a cutter component, such as a blade carrier, disc, or cutting blade assembly.

Between the drive input element and the drive output element, the shaft includes a frangible element. This frangible element is formed as a weakened portion of the shaft, such as a reduced-diameter region, groove, notch, or other intentionally weakened section. The weakened portion is positioned so that torque is normally transmitted through it from the drive input element to the drive output element during mowing operation.

The frangible element is designed to fail when the cutter unit is subjected to an excessive load, such as when the cutter strikes a stone, stump, or other obstruction. When the applied torque or shock load exceeds a predetermined limit, the weakened portion of the shaft breaks. This breakage interrupts the transmission of rotary drive from the drive input element to the drive output element, thereby helping to protect upstream drive components from damage.

The cutter unit further includes a retention mechanism that prevents the drive output element from separating from the housing after the frangible element has broken. Although the retention mechanism holds the drive output element captive relative to the housing, it still allows the drive output element to rotate. As a result, after breakage, the output side of the rotor assembly remains retained within the cutter unit rather than detaching or being ejected, while being free to turn relative to the housing. This arrangement improves safety and helps contain the cutter components in the event of an overload failure.

A rotary cutter unit for an agricultural mower is provided with a rotor shaft designed to transmit driving power from a drive input element to a drive output element that carries or drives the cutting components. The rotor shaft includes an integrated weakened, frangible portion positioned between the input side and the output side of the drive path. This frangible portion is dimensioned to act as a controlled failure point when the cutter unit is subjected to an excessive load, such as impact with a stone, stump, or other obstruction encountered during mowing.

During normal operation, torque is transmitted through the rotor shaft from the drive input element to the drive output element, causing the cutting rotor or blade assembly to rotate in the intended manner. If the load on the cutter unit exceeds a predetermined threshold, the weakened portion of the shaft fractures. This break interrupts the transmission of driving torque from the input element to the output element, thereby protecting upstream drive components, such as gearboxes, belts, shafts, and couplings, from more severe damage.

To improve safety after such a failure, the cutter unit also includes a retention mechanism that connects or restrains the drive output element relative to the cutter unit housing. The retention mechanism is arranged so that, even after the frangible portion of the rotor shaft has broken, the output element is prevented from detaching from the housing or being thrown from the machine. At the same time, the retention mechanism allows the output element to continue rotating, at least temporarily, as its remaining kinetic energy dissipates.

This arrangement provides a controlled failure system for the rotary cutter unit. The frangible shaft portion ensures that overload damage occurs at a predictable and replaceable location, while the retention mechanism keeps the failed rotating assembly contained within the cutter unit. As a result, the design reduces the risk of loose parts being ejected from the mower, improves operator and bystander safety, and limits secondary damage to the agricultural machine. The cutter unit therefore combines overload protection with post-failure containment, making it particularly suitable for agricultural mowing operations in which the cutting elements may frequently encounter hard or immovable objects.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may be small, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “the book,” we do not mean any book—we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

“The” gives clarity and direction to a sentence. It points to a person, place, object, or idea that is already known or has been mentioned before. Without it, many sentences would feel unclear or incomplete. For instance, “I saw dog” sounds unnatural, but “I saw the dog” tells us that the dog is specific.

Although “the” is simple, it appears everywhere: in stories, conversations, songs, news, and everyday speech. It connects ideas and makes communication more precise. This small word proves that even the shortest words can have a big impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a rotary cutter unit for an agricultural mower with a frangible shaft section and a retention mechanism that keeps the output element attached after failure.
counterfactuals.output: A rotary cutter unit for an agricultural mower includes a drive shaft configured to transmit torque to an output element carrying one or more cutting members. The drive shaft includes a frangible shaft section configured to fail preferentially when the rotary cutter unit is subjected to an excessive impact or overload. A retention mechanism is arranged to retain the output element on the cutter unit after failure of the frangible shaft section. The retention mechanism may include a retaining member, coupling element, tether, sleeve, fastener, or interlocking formation that remains operatively connected between a support portion of the cutter unit and the output element independently of torque transmission through the frangible shaft section. Upon overload, the frangible shaft section separates to interrupt drive to the output element while the retention mechanism prevents the output element and associated cutting members from being released from the mower. The arrangement reduces the likelihood of uncontrolled detachment of rotating components while allowing sacrificial failure to protect upstream drive components.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe in formal patent language a rotary cutter module for a mower in which overload causes a weakened shaft portion to break while a retaining element holds the cutter output element relative to the housing.
counterfactuals.output:
A rotary cutter module for a mower comprises a housing, a drive shaft rotatably supported by the housing about a cutter axis, and a cutter output element coupled to the drive shaft for rotation therewith and configured to support or drive at least one cutting blade. The drive shaft includes a torque-transmitting portion and a predetermined weakened portion located between an input region of the shaft and the cutter output element. The weakened portion is dimensioned and configured to fracture upon application of an overload torque or impact load exceeding a predetermined threshold, thereby interrupting transmission of drive from the input region to the cutter output element.

A retaining element is arranged to cooperate with the cutter output element and the housing such that, upon fracture of the weakened portion, the cutter output element is retained in a captive condition relative to the housing. The retaining element prevents separation or ejection of the cutter output element from the module while permitting the fractured shaft portion and the cutter output element to remain substantially associated with the housing after overload failure. In this manner, the weakened portion provides a sacrificial failure region for protecting upstream drive components, and the retaining element provides containment of the cutter output element following such failure.

In one embodiment, the retaining element comprises a mechanical retainer disposed axially outwardly of the cutter output element and secured relative to the housing. The mechanical retainer may include a collar, plate, ring, shoulder, fastener, circlip, or other stop member positioned to limit axial displacement of the cutter output element after rupture of the weakened shaft portion. The retaining element may define an aperture through which the shaft or a portion of the cutter output element extends, the aperture being sized to allow rotation during normal operation while restricting withdrawal of the cutter output element after failure.

The weakened portion of the shaft may comprise a reduced-diameter neck, groove, annular recess, shear section, frangible coupling region, or other stress-concentrating formation. The weakened portion is preferably located within or adjacent the housing so that fracture occurs at a controlled location. The cutter output element may comprise a blade carrier, hub, spindle output member, blade mounting disc, or blade support boss. During normal mowing operation, torque is transmitted through the weakened portion to the cutter output element. Upon the blade or cutter output element striking an obstruction, the weakened portion breaks in preference to damage to the housing, bearings, gear train, motor, belt drive, or other upstream components, while the retaining element holds the cutter output element relative to the housing.

A mower comprising such a rotary cutter module may therefore include a fail-safe cutter assembly in which overload energy is relieved by controlled fracture of a sacrificial shaft portion and in which separation of the blade carrier or cutter output element from the mower is inhibited by a dedicated retaining structure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
